name: Gyütö multiphonic chant (Tibetan Buddhist)
lineage: Tibetan Vajrayana-Buddhist Gelugpa-school tantric-chant tradition of the Gyuto Tantric University monastery (founded 1474 by Je Sherab Sengge, originally located in Lhasa, exiled 1959 to Dharamsala-and-Mysore India). The signature gyumey rang-chen multiphonic-vocal-technique produces a single chord per voice through subharmonic-overtone-isolation, with the chord typically including the fundamental, a fifth, and a major-third harmonic-overtone (heard simultaneously). Liturgical-context is the tantric sadhana practice cycle: protector-deity invocation (kangso), initiation-empowerment (wangkur), and meditation-on-tutelary-deity (yidam). The dranyen long-trumpets, gyaling oboe-like-shawms, and damaru hourglass-hand-drums punctuate the chant at canonical liturgical-points.
